verses.original: וַיָּבֹ֤א הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ וְהָמָ֔ן לִשְׁתּ֖וֹת עִם־ אֶסְתֵּ֥ר הַמַּלְכָּֽה׃
verses.literal: So the king and Haman went to dine with Esther the queen
verses.literalPt: Vieram o rei e Hamã a banquetear com a rainha Ester.

verses.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ לְאֶסְתֵּ֜ר גַּ֣ם בַּיּ֤וֹם הַשֵּׁנִי֙ בְּמִשְׁתֵּ֣ה הַיַּ֔יִן מַה־ שְּׁאֵלָתֵ֛ךְ אֶסְתֵּ֥ר הַמַּלְכָּ֖ה וְתִנָּ֣תֵֽן לָ֑ךְ וּמַה־ בַּקָּשָׁתֵ֛ךְ עַד־ חֲצִ֥י הַמַּלְכ֖וּת וְתֵעָֽשׂ׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ lə·’es·têr gam bay·yō·wm haš·šê·nî bə·miš·têh hay·ya·yin mah- šə·’ê·lā·ṯêḵ ’es·têr ham·mal·kāh wə·ṯin·nā·ṯên lāḵ ū·mah- baq·qā·šā·ṯêḵ ‘aḏ- ḥă·ṣî ham·mal·ḵūṯ wə·ṯê·‘āś
verses.literal: and as they drank their wine on that second day the king asked once more Queen Esther what is your petition It will be given to you What is your request Even up to half the kingdom it will be fulfilled
verses.literalPt: Disse o rei a Ester, também ao segundo dia durante o banquete de vinho: Qual é a tua petição, rainha Ester? E ser-te-á concedida; e qual é o teu rogo? Ainda que peças metade do reino, cumprir-se-á.

verses.original: וַתַּ֨עַן אֶסְתֵּ֤ר הַמַּלְכָּה֙ וַתֹּאמַ֔ר אִם־ מָצָ֨אתִי חֵ֤ן בְּעֵינֶ֙יךָ֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְאִם־ עַל־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ ט֑וֹב תִּנָּֽתֶן־ לִ֤י נַפְשִׁי֙ בִּשְׁאֵ֣לָתִ֔י וְעַמִּ֖י בְּבַקָּשָׁתִֽי׃
verses.transliteration: wat·ta·‘an ’es·têr ham·mal·kāh wat·tō·mar ’im- mā·ṣā·ṯî ḥên bə·‘ê·ne·ḵā ham·me·leḵ wə·’im- ‘al- ham·me·leḵ ṭō·wḇ tin·nā·ṯen- lî nap̄·šî biš·’ê·lā·ṯî wə·‘am·mî bə·ḇaq·qā·šā·ṯî
verses.literal: Queen Esther replied If I have found favor in your sight O king and if it pleases the king grant me my life as my petition and the lives of my people as my request
verses.literalPt: Ester respondeu-lhe: Se eu tiver alcançado o teu favor, ó rei, e se te parecer bem, seja-me concedida a minha vida, eis a minha petição, e a do meu povo, eis o meu rogo;

verses.original: כִּ֤י נִמְכַּ֙רְנוּ֙ אֲנִ֣י וְעַמִּ֔י לְהַשְׁמִ֖יד לַהֲר֣וֹג וּלְאַבֵּ֑ד וְ֠אִלּוּ לַעֲבָדִ֨ים וְלִשְׁפָח֤וֹת נִמְכַּ֙רְנוּ֙ הֶחֱרַ֔שְׁתִּי כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין הַצָּ֛ר שֹׁוֶ֖ה בְּנֵ֥זֶק הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ס
verses.transliteration: kî nim·kar·nū ’ă·nî wə·‘am·mî lə·haš·mîḏ la·hă·rō·wḡ ū·lə·’ab·bêḏ wə·’il·lū la·‘ă·ḇā·ḏîm wə·liš·p̄ā·ḥō·wṯ nim·kar·nū he·ḥĕ·raš·tî kî ’ên haṣ·ṣār šō·weh bə·nê·zeq ham·me·leḵ
verses.literal: For my people and I have been sold out to destruction death and annihilation If we had merely been sold as menservants and maidservants I would have remained silent because no such distress would justify burdening the king
verses.literalPt: porque fomos vendidos, eu e o meu povo, para que sejamos destruídos, mortos e pereçamos. Mas, se tivéssemos sido vendidos por escravos e por escravas, eu me teria calado, ainda que o adversário não pudesse ter compensado a injúria feita ao rei.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֔וֹשׁ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לְאֶסְתֵּ֣ר הַמַּלְכָּ֑ה מִ֣י ה֥וּא זֶה֙ וְאֵֽי־ זֶ֣ה ה֔וּא אֲשֶׁר־ מְלָא֥וֹ לִבּ֖וֹ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת כֵּֽן׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ ’ă·ḥaš·wê·rō·wōš way·yō·mer lə·’es·têr ham·mal·kāh mî hū zeh wə·’ê- zeh hū ’ă·šer- mə·lā·’ōw lib·bōw la·‘ă·śō·wṯ kên
verses.literal: Then King Xerxes spoke up and asked Queen Esther Who is this and where . . . . . . is the one who would . . . devise such a scheme?
verses.literalPt: Então, falou o rei Assuero e disse à rainha Ester: Quem é e onde está esse cujo coração o instigou a fazer isso?

verses.original: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר־ אֶסְתֵּ֔ר אִ֚ישׁ צַ֣ר וְאוֹיֵ֔ב הָמָ֥ן הָרָ֖ע הַזֶּ֑ה וְהָמָ֣ן נִבְעַ֔ת מִלִּפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְהַמַּלְכָּֽה׃
verses.transliteration: wat·tō·mer- ’es·têr ’îš ṣar wə·’ō·w·yêḇ hā·mān hā·rā‘ haz·zeh wə·hā·mān niḇ·‘aṯ mil·lip̄·nê ham·me·leḵ wə·ham·mal·kāh
verses.literal: Esther . . . replied The adversary and enemy is this wicked man Haman And Haman stood in terror before the king and queen
verses.literalPt: Respondeu Ester: Um adversário e inimigo, este maldito Hamã. Então, Hamã ficou aterrorizado perante o rei e a rainha.

verses.original: וְהַמֶּ֜לֶךְ קָ֤ם בַּחֲמָתוֹ֙ מִמִּשְׁתֵּ֣ה הַיַּ֔יִן אֶל־ גִּנַּ֖ת הַבִּיתָ֑ן וְהָמָ֣ן עָמַ֗ד לְבַקֵּ֤שׁ עַל־ נַפְשׁוֹ֙ מֵֽאֶסְתֵּ֣ר הַמַּלְכָּ֔ה כִּ֣י רָאָ֔ה כִּֽי־ כָלְתָ֥ה אֵלָ֛יו הָרָעָ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
verses.transliteration: wə·ham·me·leḵ qām ba·ḥă·mā·ṯōw mim·miš·têh hay·ya·yin ’el- gin·naṯ hab·bî·ṯān wə·hā·mān ‘ā·maḏ lə·ḇaq·qêš ‘al- nap̄·šōw mê·’es·têr ham·mal·kāh kî rā·’āh kî- ḵā·lə·ṯāh ’ê·lāw hā·rā·‘āh mê·’êṯ ham·me·leḵ
verses.literal: In his fury the king arose from drinking his wine and went to the palace garden while Haman stayed behind to beg Queen Esther for his life for he realized that the king was planning a terrible fate . . . for him
verses.literalPt: O rei, no seu furor, levantou-se do banquete de vinho e entrou no jardim do palácio. Hamã pôs-se em pé para rogar à rainha Ester pela sua vida, pois viu que já o mal lhe estava determinado pelo rei.

verses.original: וְהַמֶּ֡לֶךְ שָׁב֩ מִגִּנַּ֨ת הַבִּיתָ֜ן אֶל־ בֵּ֣ית׀ מִשְׁתֵּ֣ה הַיַּ֗יִן וְהָמָן֙ נֹפֵ֔ל עַל־ הַמִּטָּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶסְתֵּ֣ר עָלֶ֔יהָ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הֲ֠גַם לִכְבּ֧וֹשׁ אֶת־ הַמַּלְכָּ֛ה עִמִּ֖י בַּבָּ֑יִת הַדָּבָ֗ר יָצָא֙ מִפִּ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וּפְנֵ֥י הָמָ֖ן חָפֽוּ׃ס
verses.transliteration: wə·ham·me·leḵ šāḇ mig·gin·naṯ hab·bî·ṯān ’el- bêṯ miš·têh hay·ya·yin wə·hā·mān nō·p̄êl ‘al- ham·miṭ·ṭāh ’ă·šer ’es·têr ‘ā·le·hā way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ hă·ḡam liḵ·bō·wōš ’eṯ- ham·mal·kāh ‘im·mî bab·bā·yiṯ had·dā·ḇār yā·ṣā mip·pî ham·me·leḵ ū·p̄ə·nê hā·mān ḥā·p̄ū
verses.literal: Just as the king returned from the palace garden to the banquet hall . . . . . . Haman was falling on the couch where Esther was reclining The king exclaimed Would he actually assault the queen while I am in the palace As soon as the words had left the king’s mouth they covered Haman’s face
verses.literalPt: O rei voltou do jardim do palácio para o lugar do banquete de vinho; e Hamã tinha caído sobre o leito em que estava Ester. Disse o rei: Porventura, quer ele forçar a rainha na minha presença e na minha casa? Ao sair a palavra da boca do rei, cobriram a Hamã o rosto.

verses.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חַ֠רְבוֹנָה אֶחָ֨ד מִן־ הַסָּרִיסִ֜ים לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ גַּ֣ם הִנֵּה־ הָעֵ֣ץ אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֪ה הָמָ֟ן לְֽמָרְדֳּכַ֞י אֲשֶׁ֧ר דִּבֶּר־ ט֣וֹב עַל־ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ עֹמֵד֙ בְּבֵ֣ית הָמָ֔ן גָּבֹ֖הַּ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים אַמָּ֑ה וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ תְּלֻ֥הוּ עָלָֽיו׃
verses.transliteration: way·yō·mer ḥar·ḇō·w·nāh ’e·ḥāḏ min- has·sā·rî·sîm lip̄·nê ham·me·leḵ gam hin·nêh- hā·‘êṣ ’ă·šer- ‘ā·śāh hā·mān lə·mā·rə·do·ḵay ’ă·šer dib·ber- ṭō·wḇ ‘al- ham·me·leḵ ‘ō·mêḏ bə·ḇêṯ hā·mān gā·ḇō·ah ḥă·miš·šîm ’am·māh way·yō·mer ham·me·leḵ tə·lu·hū ‘ā·lāw
verses.literal: Then Harbonah one of the eunuchs attending the king . . . said There is a gallows fifty cubits high at Haman’s house He had it built for Mordecai who gave the report that saved . . . the king . . . Hang him on it declared the king
verses.literalPt: Disse Harbona, um dos eunucos que serviam o rei: Eis que existe na casa de Hamã a forca que tem cinquenta cúbitos de altura, a qual Hamã tinha preparado para Mordecai, que falou em defesa do rei. Disse o rei: Pendurai-o nela.

verses.original: וַיִּתְלוּ֙ אֶת־ הָמָ֔ן עַל־ הָעֵ֖ץ אֲשֶׁר־ הֵכִ֣ין לְמָרְדֳּכָ֑י וַחֲמַ֥ת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ שָׁכָֽכָה׃פ
verses.transliteration: way·yiṯ·lū ’eṯ- hā·mān ‘al- hā·‘êṣ ’ă·šer- hê·ḵîn lə·mā·rə·do·ḵāy wa·ḥă·maṯ ham·me·leḵ šā·ḵā·ḵāh
verses.literal: So they hanged Haman on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai Then the fury of the king subsided
verses.literalPt: Penduraram a Hamã na forca que ele tinha preparado para Mordecai. Então, se aplacou o furor do rei.
